audienceSegments: Daily commuters grabbing coffee on the way to work
Remote workers and students using stores as a 'third place'
Gen Z social and seasonal-drink fans
keyFacts: Largest coffeehouse company in the world; 34,000+ stores across 84 markets
Founded 1971 as a roaster/retailer in Seattle's Pike Place Market; named after the first mate in Moby Dick
Public since 1992 (NASDAQ: SBUX); brand portfolio includes Seattle's Best Coffee, Teavana, Evolution Fresh, Ethos Water
'Back to Starbucks' turnaround under CEO Brian Niccol (joined 2024): smaller-format store prototypes, 1,000 store 'uplifts' by end of 2026, $1B+ invested in customer experience
Plans ~5,000 new US cafes over the next few years with a smaller, 20%-cheaper-to-build format
marketingChannels: Starbucks Rewards loyalty program and mobile app
In-store 'third place' experience and community events
products: Fresh food: pastries, sandwiches, protein boxes
tagline: To inspire and nurture the human spirit — one person, one cup and one neighborhood at a time
